text:
kevin: Heads up — intermittent packet drops on vxlan overlay in gpu-pool-usw2. p99 tail latency spikes for gen requests, started ~10:12 UTC.
opsbot: [ALERT] INF_PACKET_LOSS triggered for cluster-gpu-usw2 (overlay-soft-drop rule)
maria: saw this too, only during backfills. Not all nodes. Seems concentrated on hw-mlx5-05..07.
jonathan: ran tcpdump on hw-mlx5-05, bursts of retransmits and dup acks. small frames, lots of segs.
sophie: are the affected pods using rdma? i've seen geneve + offload interactions bite us before.
kevin: yes, RDMA-enabled IMDS experiments and model loaders. GSO/TSO still enabled on hosts.
maria: can you paste ethtool and ip link? want to check offload + mtu mismatch across encap path.
jonathan: pasted samples:
```
$ ethtool -k eth0
finding out capabilities...
rx-checksumming: on
large-receive-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
offload-params: tso on gso on
$ ip link show dev genev0
4: genev0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff
```
maria: mtu 1450 on geneve looks right for 1500 underlay with 50 bytes overhead, but some hosts show 1500 on geneve. mismatch -> fragmentation.
sophie: fragmentation + GSO can cause tiny frames when offload is incorrectly applied before encap. we saw similar in INF-924.
kevin: quick workaround idea: disable GSO on NICs for nodes in affected pool and retest.
jonathan: quick repro: iperf3 between pods shows 0.1-0.5% loss during backfill, and Ctrl-C shows retransmits increasing.
maria: commands to toggle offload if we want to try on one node:
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off gro off
# restart kube-proxy/pod network? not needed, offload is host-level
```
sophie: agree do one node as canary. also collect pcap on veth + genev0 to see pre/post-encap sizes.
kevin: i'll spin up a canary and run these steps:
- disable GSO/TSO/GRO on hw-mlx5-05
- run backfill workload (replay of recent traffic)
- collect tcpdump on eth0 + genev0 + veth inside pod
- measure p99 latency and retransmit counts
maria: tagging this INF-1037, adding logs + pcap to the ticket. cc @sre oncall for paging if it escalates.
opsbot: Incident INF-1037 created by kevin — severity P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INF-1037
jonathan: initial canary results: after disabling offloads on hw-mlx5-05, retransmits dropped by ~80% during identical workload. p99 latency normalized.
sophie: good signal. that points to offload+encap ordering bug in mlx5 kernel driver or the RDMA stack. we should test kernel versions.
kevin: plan: (1) roll through affected nodes with offloads disabled (2) schedule vendor debug with Mellanox/driver team (3) patch kube-proxy/networking to enforce MTU on all hosts to avoid mismatch.
maria: are there cost/throughput regressions with offloads disabled? we need to measure CPU overhead.
jonathan: short test shows ~6% CPU increase on host net stack, within acceptable SLAs for now. will quantify.
kevin: creating a short runbook for oncall: how to detect, how to toggle offloads, how to roll back. adding commands + safe checks.
sophie: also add a mitigation in the control plane: when backfill comms detected across gpu pool, prefer nodes with same driver/mtu fingerprint. might be a quick routing policy.
maria: assigned to infra eng to schedule driver debug and kernel bisect. target: next week.
kevin: thanks all. if anyone sees recurrence after we finish the roll, escalate to P1. For now, canary looks promising. :thumbsup:
